title: Dreaming Up Authors: Factual Prevalence and LLM Hallucinations in Academic Authorship Attribution
abstract: arXiv:2611.23530v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely used for question answering but are prone to hallucinations, yet the underlying causes, particularly the role of factual prevalence in training data, remain underexplored. In this work, we study this through academic authorship attribution, hypothesizing that hallucinations are more likely for less prevalent papers. Using citation count as a proxy for factual prevalence, we curate a dataset of 1.92 million papers across eight scientific disciplines with stratified samples by citation level. Experiments on three state-of-the-art LLMs confirm our hypothesis, revealing a robust inverse relationship between hallucination rate and citation count across all models and disciplines, with hallucination rates exceeding 98% for rarely cited papers and falling below 37% for highly cited ones. translated_title: 凭空虚构作者：学术作者归属中的事实普遍性与大语言模型幻觉
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）被广泛用于问答任务，但容易产生幻觉，然而其背后的根本原因，特别是训练数据中事实普遍性的作用，仍未得到充分探索。在本工作中，我们通过学术作者归属任务来研究这一问题，假设对于流行度较低的论文，模型更容易产生幻觉。我们使用论文引用次数作为事实普遍性的代理指标，构建了一个涵盖八个科学学科、共计192万篇论文的数据集，并按引用水平进行分层抽样。在三个最先进大语言模型上的实验证实了我们的假设，揭示了幻觉率与引用次数之间在所有模型和学科上都稳健存在的反比关系：低引用论文的幻觉率超过98%，而高引用论文的幻觉率则低于37%。我们的深入分析进一步表明，这些失败主要反映了检索能力的局限，而非知识的缺失（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该研究通过192万篇论文的作者归属实验发现，论文引用量与大语言模型幻觉率呈稳健的反比关系——低引用论文幻觉率超过98%，高引用论文低于37%，且失败主要源于检索局限而非知识缺失。
en_tdlr: This study, based on authorship attribution experiments across 1.92 million papers, reveals a robust inverse relationship between paper citation counts and LLM hallucination rates—exceeding 98% for rarely cited papers and falling below 37% for highly cited ones—with failures primarily stemming from retrieval limitations rather than knowledge absence.
